decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: What identity documents must every New Jersey driver license applicant have?
cards.back: Every applicant for a New Jersey driver license must have all the documents needed to satisfy the six-Point ID Verification.

cards.front: What vision requirement applies to every motorist, and what may the MVC do about impaired vision?
cards.back: Every motorist must pass a vision screening; the MVC may send applicants with impaired vision to a physician and may periodically require a recheck.

cards.front: What vision do basic license applicants need?
cards.back: Basic license applicants need twenty over fifty vision, with or without corrective lenses.

cards.front: What must an applicant who sees with only one eye show?
cards.back: An applicant who sees with only one eye must have that eye meet the twenty over fifty rule and bring documentation signed by a licensed physician.
cards.memory_hook: one eye, same rule, doctor's note

cards.front: What vision and color standard must CDL applicants meet?
cards.back: CDL applicants need twenty over forty vision in both eyes, with or without corrective lenses, and must tell red, green and amber lights apart.

cards.front: How does basic license vision differ from CDL vision?
cards.back: Basic license applicants need twenty over fifty vision with or without corrective lenses, while CDL applicants need twenty over forty in both eyes plus the ability to tell red, green and amber lights apart.

cards.front: What forms must commercial drivers file under federal law and New Jersey rules?
cards.back: Federal law and New Jersey rules require commercial drivers to file a CDL Holder Self-Certification form and, if applicable, a medical examiner's certificate completed by a federally certified medical examiner.

cards.front: What must applicants tell the examiner about their health, and what may follow?
cards.back: Applicants must tell the examiner about health problems, and a medical review may be necessary.

decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: What does the knowledge test contain besides its regular questions?
cards.back: The knowledge test has fifty questions, plus a survey question about organ donation.

cards.front: What does it take to pass the written test?
cards.back: To pass the written test, eighty percent of the answers must be correct, which is forty of the fifty questions.

cards.front: In which languages is the knowledge test offered?
cards.back: The knowledge test is offered in English and American Sign Language, and also in Albanian, Arabic, Chinese, French, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish.

cards.front: How does an applicant who cannot read in any language take the knowledge test?
cards.back: An applicant who cannot read in any language is given headphones and takes the knowledge test orally.

cards.front: When may you use a state-approved interpreter for the knowledge test?
cards.back: If your native language is not offered you may use a state-approved interpreter, but only after first attempting the test in one of the offered languages.

cards.front: How much notice must an applicant who needs an interpreter give the MVC?
cards.back: An applicant who needs an interpreter must tell the MVC at least two weeks before the planned date of the written knowledge test.

cards.front: What two conditions come before an interpreter for an unlisted language is arranged?
cards.back: The knowledge test language list includes American Sign Language, but a state-approved interpreter for an unlisted language is arranged only after a failed attempt in an offered language and with at least two weeks' notice.

cards.front: What does the MVC provide and pay for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants?
cards.back: The MVC provides approved interpreters for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants and pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees once a completed payment voucher form is submitted.

cards.front: Who counts as an approved foreign-language interpreter?
cards.back: An approved foreign-language interpreter is someone listed on the Registry of Interpreters and Agencies kept by the NJ Administrative Office of the Courts, Language Services Section.

cards.front: Who counts as an approved deaf or hard of hearing interpreter?
cards.back: An approved deaf or hard of hearing interpreter either holds certification from the National Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf and is on file with the NJ Division of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, or has been evaluated by that Division and placed on its approved list.

cards.front: What happens once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, and how are Deaf or Hard of Hearing interpreter fees handled?
cards.back: Once a foreign-language interpreter is secured, an MVC employee contacts the applicant with the appointment date and time, while for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants the MVC pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees after a payment voucher form.

decks.module: Transfers from other states and countries
decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: Which transfer applicants may have the knowledge and road tests waived?
cards.back: Knowledge and road tests may be waived for transfer applicants aged eighteen or older with a valid, non-provisional license from any of the fifty states, the District of Columbia, Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico or the US Virgin Islands.

cards.front: What does a transfer applicant still submit, receive and give up?
cards.back: Transfer applicants still submit the six-Point ID documents, receive a four-year basic New Jersey license and must surrender the out-of-state license.

cards.front: What license does an out-of-state applicant aged seventeen to eighteen receive?
cards.back: An out-of-state applicant aged seventeen to eighteen with a valid license receives a probationary license for one year and must follow New Jersey's GDL rules.

cards.front: How does an adult transfer differ from a seventeen-to-eighteen transfer?
cards.back: A transfer applicant aged eighteen or older with a valid non-provisional license gets a four-year basic license, while one aged seventeen to eighteen gets a probationary license for one year under GDL rules.

cards.front: What must every out-of-country applicant pass, and how long are the results valid?
cards.back: Every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening and may also have to pass a road test; the results are valid for two years.

cards.front: How do testing rules differ for out-of-state and out-of-country applicants?
cards.back: Out-of-state transfer applicants may have the knowledge and road tests waived, but every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening.

decks.module: Nikhil's Law, voting and your address
decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: What did Nikhil's Law change, and when did it take effect?
cards.back: Signed in August two thousand fifteen and in force from March one, two thousand sixteen, Nikhil's Law amended N.J.S.A. thirty-nine:three-forty-one to stress the dangers of ignoring New Jersey traffic laws.

cards.front: What does the Safety Pledge to Nikhil commit drivers to do?
cards.back: The Safety Pledge to Nikhil commits drivers to stop completely, stay alert, talk safe with a hands-free system and plan ahead by allowing an extra five minutes for every trip.

cards.front: Where can eligible voters start voter registration, and what is the deadline?
cards.back: Eligible voters can start voter registration at any MVC Licensing Center while applying for or renewing a license or non-driver ID, and the registration deadline is twenty-one days before an election.

cards.front: How can someone not doing a license or ID transaction register to vote?
cards.back: Someone not doing a license or ID transaction can still register to vote or change a voting address through the New Jersey Division of Elections, which can mail an application.

cards.front: How must address changes be done, and what does the MVC then ask?
cards.back: Address changes must be done online, and the MVC then asks whether the change should also update your voter record.

cards.front: Where does the MVC forward address changes, and whom do you contact if no confirmation arrives?
cards.back: Address changes reported to the MVC online or by mail are forwarded to the New Jersey Division of Elections, and you should contact your local Commissioner of Registration if no confirmation arrives.

cards.front: What address does the law require you to give the MVC, and how do you get a license showing it?
cards.back: The law requires you to give the MVC your current New Jersey home address, and a replacement license showing the new address can be ordered after the change is processed.

decks.module: Permit practice before the road test
decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: When does the MVC validate the permit for practice driving?
cards.back: Once the knowledge test, vision screening and any required behind-the-wheel course are passed, the MVC validates the permit for practice driving.

cards.front: How much supervised practice do GDL permit holders under twenty-one need before a road test appointment?
cards.back: GDL permit holders under twenty-one need at least six months of supervised practice with at least fifty hours, ten of them in darkness, before a road test appointment.
cards.memory_hook: six months, fifty hours, ten dark

cards.front: How much supervised practice do GDL permit holders aged twenty-one or older need before a road test appointment?
cards.back: GDL permit holders aged twenty-one or older need at least three months of supervised practice before a road test appointment.

cards.front: How do the practice minimums differ for permit holders under twenty-one and those twenty-one and older?
cards.back: Before a road test appointment, GDL permit holders under twenty-one need six months and at least fifty supervised hours with ten after dark, while those twenty-one and older need only three months.

cards.front: What form must be presented at the road test appointment, and who completes it?
cards.back: A completed BA-CSD form from a parent, guardian or supervising driver must be presented at the time of the road test appointment.

cards.front: Where is practice driving not allowed?
cards.back: Practice driving is not allowed on the road test course or in the parallel parking area.

decks.module: What to bring and who rides along
decks.domain: Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test

cards.front: Which original documents must road test applicants bring?
cards.back: Road test applicants must bring original documents: six points of ID, a legible unlaminated validated permit, a valid inspection sticker or the official card saying none is required, and valid registration and insurance ID cards for the test vehicle.

cards.front: What must GDL applicants also have on the test vehicle?
cards.back: GDL applicants must also have two red GDL decals properly mounted on the test vehicle.

cards.front: What must a test vehicle registered in another state meet?
cards.back: A test vehicle registered in another state must meet that home state's insurance identification laws.

cards.front: When is a rental car allowed for the road test?
cards.back: A rental car is allowed only if the applicant is named as a driver on the rental agreement, and the applicant must arrive with a licensed driver.

cards.front: When must a licensed driver be in the vehicle with the applicant?
cards.back: A licensed driver must stay in the vehicle with the applicant at all times, and the car may not be moved even in the road test line without one.

cards.front: When must the accompanying driver drive the vehicle to the road test area?
cards.back: If the accompanying driver is licensed outside New Jersey or has under three years of experience, that person must drive the vehicle to the road test area.

cards.front: Who supplies the road test vehicle, and who may be in it during the test?
cards.back: The MVC does not supply road test vehicles, and only MVC examiners may be in the vehicle during the test.

decks.module: When the test vehicle is rejected
decks.domain: Testing confusables and road test vehicle rules

cards.front: Is only your driving graded at the road test?
cards.back: Many applicants assume only their driving is graded, but the vehicle itself can cause a denial, and an examiner may refuse even an initial road test in an unsuitable or unsafe car.

cards.front: Which brake must the examiner be able to reach?
cards.back: The examiner must be able to reach the foot brake or a parking brake mounted to the right of the driver.

cards.front: Which vehicles cannot be used for the road test, and what equipment must work?
cards.back: Autocycles and self-parking vehicles cannot be used, and the signals, brake lights and windshield wipers must all work.

cards.front: What are common reasons a road test vehicle is rejected?
cards.back: Common road test vehicle rejections include an improper, expired or missing inspection sticker, no examiner access to a brake, poor brakes, a lit brake warning light and unsafe tires.

cards.front: When is a vehicle that failed inspection still accepted, and why is a fast engine idle rejected?
cards.back: A vehicle that failed inspection is rejected unless the motorist brings the Vehicle Inspection Report from the inspection station, and a fast engine idle is rejected because speed control cannot be judged.

cards.front: Why does a test vehicle with missing seat belts get rejected?
cards.back: Seat belts are required on all vehicles manufactured after July one, nineteen sixty-six, so missing belts get a test vehicle rejected.

cards.front: Which glass, tint, mirror and door problems get a test vehicle rejected?
cards.back: Window tint on the driver or front door windows, missing interior or driver-door mirrors, broken or cracked glass, and doors or windows that will not work from inside all get a vehicle rejected.

cards.front: What brake, light and interior conditions must a test vehicle meet?
cards.back: Brakes must not fade or sink to the floorboard, the parking brake, brake lights and signal lights must work, and the interior must be reasonably clean.

cards.front: Which extra problems cause rejection only for motorcycle and moped tests?
cards.back: For motorcycle and moped tests only, missing state-required equipment, no helmet, unapproved goggles or face shield, or no bell or horn audible at one hundred feet also cause rejection.

decks.module: Road test skills and your license
decks.domain: Testing confusables and road test vehicle rules

cards.front: Where does the examiner ride with you during the road test, and why?
cards.back: During the road test an MVC examiner rides with the applicant in an off-road test area or on a public road course to confirm the applicant knows the rules and drives safely.

cards.front: What will the examiner ask if the test vehicle has a standard transmission?
cards.back: If the test vehicle has a standard transmission, the examiner will ask the applicant to show correct gear shifting.

cards.front: What does the basic road test cover?
cards.back: The basic road test covers driving in reverse, following other vehicles, nearing corners and intersections, parallel parking, sitting properly with a seat belt, starting, steering, stopping at signs, stopping smoothly, turning, turning around, using the horn and yielding right-of-way.

cards.front: What do you receive after passing the road test, and where do you take it?
cards.back: After passing the road test you receive an authorization for licensing, and the permit, the authorization and six Points of ID must be taken to a Licensing Center.

cards.front: What license does an applicant never before licensed anywhere receive, and what does the MVC do for one year?
cards.back: An applicant never before licensed anywhere receives a Class D basic or probationary license, and the MVC monitors that driver's habits for one year.

recap_hooks.text: Every applicant brings six-point ID, and REAL ID adds two address proofs and one Social Security proof.
Basic license vision is twenty-fifty, a single seeing eye must meet it with a physician's note, and CDL vision is twenty-forty in both eyes with color recognition.
Tell the examiner about health problems, since a medical review may follow.
The knowledge test also carries a survey question about organ donation, and passing depends on the share of answers you get right.
The test comes in English, American Sign Language and a long list of other languages, and someone who cannot read takes it orally with headphones.
An interpreter for an unlisted language comes only after trying an offered language, with two weeks' notice to the MVC.

recaps.module: Transfers from other states and countries

recap_hooks.text: Adults with a valid, non-provisional license from another state may skip the tests and get a four-year basic license after surrendering the old one.
Seventeen-to-eighteen transfers get a one-year probationary license, and out-of-country applicants must pass the knowledge test and vision screening.

recaps.module: Nikhil's Law, voting and your address

recap_hooks.text: Nikhil's Law stresses the dangers of ignoring traffic laws, and the Safety Pledge asks you to stop completely, stay alert, talk hands-free and plan ahead.
You can start voter registration at a Licensing Center, address changes go online, and the MVC must always have your current home address.

recaps.module: Permit practice before the road test

recap_hooks.text: Under twenty-one, practice at least six months and fifty hours with ten in darkness; at twenty-one or older, at least three months.
Bring the completed BA-CSD form, and never practice on the test course or in the parallel parking area.

recaps.module: What to bring and who rides along

recap_hooks.text: Bring original ID, an unlaminated validated permit, an inspection sticker, registration and insurance cards, plus two red decals for GDL drivers.
A licensed driver stays with you even in the test line, but during the test only the examiner rides along.

recaps.module: When the test vehicle is rejected

recap_hooks.text: The car itself can end your road test before it starts, so check it first.
Expect a rejection for a bad inspection sticker, weak brakes, a lit brake warning light, unsafe tires or missing seat belts.
Clear glass, working mirrors, doors and lights, and a clean interior keep the car in the test.

recaps.module: Road test skills and your license

recap_hooks.text: The basic road test checks reversing, parallel parking, turning, stopping and yielding, plus gear shifting in a standard car.
After passing, take the authorization, permit and six points of ID to a Licensing Center; never-licensed drivers are monitored for one year.

merges.justification: sec03-F02 restates the sec03-F01 six-point ID requirement for REAL ID applicants; its accepted wording uses plus symbols that cannot be spoken as a card back, so the sec03-F01 card carries both.
